blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: The Secret of Roman Concrete
blocks.body:
Many buildings made by the ancient Romans are still standing today, nearly 2,000 years after they were built. The Pantheon in Rome, for example, still has the world's largest dome made of concrete without steel inside it. Modern concrete, in contrast, often begins to crack after only 50 to 100 years. For a long time, scientists ( 18 ).
In 2023, a team of researchers found an important clue. Roman concrete contains small white pieces of lime. Earlier scientists believed that these pieces were simply a sign of ( 19 ). However, the new research showed that they play a key role. When a crack forms and water gets inside, the lime dissolves and then hardens again, filling the crack. In other words, the concrete can repair itself.
Engineers now hope to use this idea to make modern concrete last longer. ( 20 ), producing concrete releases a large amount of carbon dioxide, so concrete that does not need to be replaced often could also help protect the environment.

o: built new roads using Roman methods
believed that Roman buildings were made of stone
wondered why Roman concrete lasted so long
qs.ex: 現代のコンクリートは50〜100年でひびが入るのに、ローマのものは2000年もつ→「なぜ長持ちするのか不思議に思っていた」。
However で「実は重要な役割があった」と続くので、以前は「混ぜ方が悪かったしるし」と考えられていた。
長持ちする利点に「さらに」環境にも良い、という追加なので Moreover。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Forest Bathing
blocks.body:
In the 1980s, Japan's Forestry Agency began to promote a practice called shinrin-yoku, or "forest bathing." The idea is simple: people walk slowly through a forest and enjoy the sights, sounds, and smells around them. Unlike hiking, the purpose is not to reach a goal or ( 21 ).
Since then, researchers have studied the effects of forest bathing on health. In several studies, people who spent time in forests had lower blood pressure and lower levels of stress hormones than people who walked in cities. Some scientists believe that ( 22 ). Trees release natural chemicals into the air, and breathing them may help the body relax.
Today, forest bathing has spread to many countries, including the United States and the United Kingdom. ( 23 ), some doctors now recommend spending time in nature to patients who suffer from stress.

qs.ex: ハイキングとちがい、目的地に着くことや「運動すること」が目的ではありません。

o: the air in forests plays a role
stress has no effect on health
qs.ex: 次の文の「木が空気中に出す自然の化学物質」が説明になっているので、「森の空気が関係している」。
世界に広まった→「実際に」医師がすすめるほどになっている、と強める流れ。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.body:
From: Blue Horizon Airways
To: Kaito Mori
Date: July 28
Subject: Change to your flight BH 207

Dear Mr. Mori,
We are writing to inform you that the departure time of your flight, BH 207 from Tokyo to Vancouver on August 10, has been changed. Because of a change in airport schedules, the flight will now leave at 9:40 p.m. instead of 6:15 p.m. As a result, it will arrive in Vancouver at 2:25 p.m. local time, about three and a half hours later than originally planned.
We understand that this change may cause you inconvenience. If the new time is not suitable for you, you can change to another flight on a different day at no extra cost, or you can cancel your booking and receive a full refund. Please let us know your decision through the "My Booking" page on our website by August 3.
If you choose to keep your booking, you do not need to do anything. As a small token of our apology, all passengers on this flight will receive a voucher for 3,000 yen that can be used at restaurants in the departure area of the airport.
We apologize for any trouble this may cause.
Blue Horizon Airways Customer Service

qs.q: Why has the flight time been changed?
o: The plane needs to be repaired.
The weather will be bad on August 10.
qs.ex: Because of a change in airport schedules とあります。

qs.q: What should Mr. Mori do if he wants a refund?
o: Go to the airport by August 10.
Tell the airline on its website by August 3.
Send an email to the restaurant.
qs.ex: 「My Booking」ページで8月3日までに知らせます。

qs.q: What will passengers who keep their booking receive?
o: A free hotel room in Vancouver.
qs.ex: 空港の出発エリアのレストランで使える3,000円の券がもらえます。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Learning to Fly Without Leaving the Ground
blocks.body:
Before pilots fly a new type of passenger plane, they spend many hours in a flight simulator. A modern full-flight simulator is a large box that sits on six powerful legs. Inside is an exact copy of a real cockpit, with the same seats, screens, and controls. The legs move the box so that pilots feel the plane speed up, turn, and shake, while screens outside the windows show realistic views of airports and cities around the world.
Simulators have several advantages over training in real airplanes. First, they are much cheaper to operate, because they do not use fuel. Second, and more importantly, they allow pilots to practice dealing with emergencies that would be far too dangerous to create in real life, such as an engine fire during takeoff or a sudden storm. Instructors can choose the problem, the weather, and even the time of day with a few clicks.
Simulators are so realistic today that, in many countries, pilots who already have experience can qualify to fly a new type of airliner after training only in a simulator. The first time they fly the real plane, there may be passengers on board, although an experienced training captain sits next to them.
Pilots must also return to the simulator regularly throughout their careers. Most airline pilots have checks at least once or twice a year, in which they must show that they can still handle emergencies correctly. Many pilots say these checks are the most stressful part of the job, but they also agree that such training has helped make flying one of the safest ways to travel.

qs.q: What is true about a full-flight simulator?
o: It is a small model of an airplane.
It can actually fly short distances.
It can move so that pilots feel the plane's movement.
qs.ex: The legs move the box so that pilots feel the plane speed up, turn, and shake とあります。

qs.q: What is the most important advantage of simulators?
o: They use less fuel than real planes.
Pilots can safely practice dealing with emergencies.
They show views of cities around the world.
qs.ex: and more importantly のあとに「危険な緊急事態の練習ができる」とあります。燃料は一つ目の利点です。

qs.q: Experienced pilots in many countries can
o: skip training for a new type of plane.
fly passengers without a training captain.
qualify for a new type of airliner after training only in a simulator.
qs.ex: can qualify to fly a new type of airliner after training only in a simulator とあります。

qs.q: How often do most airline pilots have checks in the simulator?
o: At least once or twice a year.
Only when they start their careers.
qs.ex: checks at least once or twice a year とあります。

qs.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: Simulators are more expensive to operate than real planes.
Instructors cannot change the weather in a simulator.
Pilots think simulator checks are easy.
Pilots believe simulator training has helped make flying safer.
qs.ex: they also agree that such training has helped make flying one of the safest ways to travel とあります。

parts.prompt:
以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。
語数の目安は45語〜55語です。
parts.body:
In recent years, some companies in Japan have started allowing their employees to take "workations." The word combines "work" and "vacation." Workers stay at a hotel or a rented house in a resort area, such as a beach town or a hot spring village, and work there online during the day.
Supporters say that workations are good for both workers and companies. Working in a relaxing environment can reduce stress and help people come up with new ideas. Local towns also welcome workations because visitors spend money at shops and restaurants, even on weekdays.
However, workations also have some disadvantages. It can be hard for workers to separate their work time from their free time, so some end up working too much. In addition, the internet connection in some areas is not good enough for online meetings.
rules: 解答は、英文要約の解答欄に書きなさい。なお、解答欄の外に書かれたものは採点されません。
要約の内容が英文から逸れていると判断された場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。英文をよく読んでから答えてください。
parts.model: Some Japanese companies now let workers take workations, working online from resort areas. These can reduce stress, inspire new ideas, and bring money to local towns. However, workers may find it hard to separate work from free time, and poor internet connections can cause problems for online meetings.
checks: 第1段落(ワーケーションとは何か)の内容が入っている
第2段落の利点(ストレス軽減・アイデア・地域にお金)が入っている
第3段落の問題点(仕事と休みの区別・ネット環境)が入っている
本文の表現を言いかえて短くまとめている(However などで対比)
語数が45〜55語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英文要約)

parts.prompt:
以下のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。
POINTSは理由を書く際の参考となる観点を示したものです。ただし、これら以外の観点から理由を書いてもかまいません。

TOPIC
Some people say that schools should stop using their own swimming pools and use public pools instead. Do you agree with this opinion?

POINTS
・Cost
・Safety
・Convenience
rules: 語数の目安は80語〜100語です。
理由は2つ書きましょう。
TOPICに示された問いに答えていない場合や、内容がTOPICからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model: I agree that schools should use public pools instead of their own. I have two reasons. First, it would save a lot of money. School pools are used for only a few months each year, but cleaning and repairing them is very expensive. Schools could use that money for computers or books. Second, public pools are often safer. They have professional lifeguards and instructors, so students can learn to swim more effectively. For these reasons, I think using public pools is a better choice for schools.
checks: 最初に賛成か反対かをはっきり書いている
理由を2つ書き、それぞれに具体的な説明がある
POINTSの観点(費用・安全など)を使っている
最後に結論をもう一度書いている
語数が80〜100語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Hi, I'd like to rent a car for three days, starting tomorrow.
Certainly. We have small cars and minivans available. How many people will be traveling?
Five adults, and we'll have a lot of luggage.
Then I'd recommend a minivan. It's a little more expensive, but it'll be much more comfortable.
items.q: What will the man rent?
items.ex: 大人5人と荷物が多いので、すすめられたミニバンにしました。

lines: Excuse me, I think there's a mistake on my bill. I only ordered one coffee, but I was charged for two.
I'm so sorry about that. Let me check. You're right. I'll correct it right away.
And please accept this free cookie for the trouble.
items.q: What was the problem?
o: The café was out of cookies.
items.ex: コーヒー1杯なのに2杯分請求されていました。

lines: Did you see the notice about the new parking rules at the office?
Starting next month, employees will have to pay 5,000 yen a month to park in the company parking lot.
Really? Then I might start taking the train. The station is only a ten-minute walk from my house.
items.q: What might the woman do?
items.ex: I might start taking the train. と言っています。

lines: Hi, Ken. How was your first week at your new job?
Busy, but I'm enjoying it. My coworkers are really friendly.
That's great. Is it far from your house?
It takes about an hour by train, so I'm thinking of moving closer to the office this summer.
items.q: What is Ken thinking of doing this summer?
items.ex: I'm thinking of moving closer to the office this summer. と言っています。

lines: Excuse me, I'm looking for a book about the history of aviation for my son. He wants to become a pilot.

o: A book about the history of airplanes.
A guide to becoming a pilot.
A ticket for an air show.
items.ex: a book about the history of aviation(航空の歴史の本)をさがしています。

lines: Dad, can I borrow your laptop this weekend? Mine is broken.
I need it for work on Saturday morning. You can use it in the afternoon, though.
Thanks. I just need to finish a presentation for school.
OK, but don't forget to save your files on a USB stick.
items.q: When can the girl use the laptop?
items.ex: 土曜の朝は父が仕事で使うので、午後なら使えます。

lines: How was the musical last night?
The singing was wonderful, but our seats were so far from the stage that we couldn't see the actors' faces.
That's too bad. Did you buy the tickets online?
Yes, they were cheap, but next time I'll pay more for better seats.
items.q: What will the woman do next time?
items.ex: next time I'll pay more for better seats と言っています。

lines: Hello, this is Green Dental Clinic. I'm calling to remind you about your appointment tomorrow at 10 a.m.
Oh, thank you. Actually, I have an important meeting tomorrow morning. Can I change it to the afternoon?
Let me see. We have an opening at 4 p.m.
items.q: When will the man go to the dentist?
items.ex: 午前は会議なので、明日の午後4時に変更しました。

lines: Mary, you're a good cook. Could you teach me how to make gyoza?
Sure. It's not difficult. When are you free?
OK. Come to my place at two, and bring the vegetables. I'll get the meat.
items.q: What will the man bring?
items.ex: bring the vegetables と言われています。肉は女性が用意します。

lines: Excuse me, sir. You can't take that large bag into the gallery.
Oh, I didn't know. Where can I leave it?
There are lockers next to the entrance. They cost 100 yen, but you get the coin back when you open them again.
items.q: What will the man probably do?
o: Put his bag in a locker.
Carry the bag in his hand.
items.ex: 入口の横のロッカーにかばんを預けるでしょう。

lines: Have you started looking for a new apartment yet?
Yes, but everything near the university is too expensive.
What about sharing a place with someone? My friend is looking for a roommate.
That might work. Could you introduce me to her?
items.q: What does the man suggest?
items.ex: sharing a place with someone(だれかと部屋をシェアする)を提案しています。

lines: Jim, the client meeting has been moved from Tuesday to Thursday.
Thursday? I'm going on a business trip to Sapporo that day.
Oh no. Can you ask Mr. Sato to go to Sapporo instead?
I'll try. Otherwise, I'll join the meeting online from the hotel.
items.q: What will Jim do first?
o: Ask Mr. Sato to go to Sapporo.
items.ex: まず佐藤さんに札幌へ行ってもらえるか頼み、だめならオンラインで参加します。

lines: Mom, our school is looking for families to host exchange students from Australia next month.
That sounds interesting. How long would the student stay?
Two weeks. Can we do it? I want to practice my English.
Let me talk with your father tonight first.
items.q: What will the mother do tonight?
items.ex: Let me talk with your father tonight first. と言っています。

lines: Excuse me, how do I get to the Science Museum?
Take the subway to Park Station. It's right next to the exit.
Is it far to walk from here?
It's about 30 minutes, but the subway only takes ten.
items.q: How will the man go to the museum?
items.ex: Then I'll take the subway. と言っています。

lines: Have you heard that the café downstairs is closing?
Really? I go there every morning for coffee.
The owner is retiring. A bakery will open there next month.
Well, at least I'll still be able to get breakfast.
items.q: Why is the café closing?
items.ex: The owner is retiring. と言っています。

lines: Kaori has been learning to play the violin since she was six. Last year, she joined a youth orchestra in her city. The orchestra practices every Sunday and gives concerts twice a year. This spring, Kaori was chosen to play a solo at the concert, and she has been practicing for hours every day.
items.q: What will Kaori do at the spring concert?
items.ex: Kaori was chosen to play a solo at the concert とあります。

lines: Attention, passengers traveling to Singapore on Flight 718. Boarding will begin in ten minutes. Passengers with small children and those who need extra help will be invited to board first. Please have your boarding pass and passport ready.
items.q: Who will be invited to board first?
items.ex: Passengers with small children and those who need extra help will be invited to board first とあります。

lines: Polar bears look white, but their skin is actually black. Their fur is not really white either. Each hair is clear and hollow, and it looks white because it reflects light. Their black skin helps them absorb heat from the sun.
items.q: What helps polar bears absorb heat from the sun?
items.ex: Their black skin helps them absorb heat from the sun. とあります。

lines: When Jun started high school, he had trouble waking up in the morning. His older sister told him to stop using his smartphone an hour before going to bed. Jun tried it, and he soon found that he could fall asleep more quickly and wake up more easily.
items.q: What did Jun's sister tell him to do?
o: Stop using his phone before bed.
items.ex: 寝る1時間前にスマートフォンを使うのをやめるよう言いました。

lines: Welcome to Green Lake Park. Today, boats can be rented at the boathouse until 5 p.m. Please note that swimming in the lake is not allowed. Also, a fireworks show will be held tonight at 8 p.m., so the park will stay open until 9.
items.q: What will happen tonight at 8 p.m.?
o: A fireworks show will be held.
items.ex: a fireworks show will be held tonight at 8 p.m. とあります。

lines: In the early 20th century, many people believed that flying across the Atlantic Ocean alone was impossible. In 1927, Charles Lindbergh proved them wrong. He flew from New York to Paris without stopping in about 33 and a half hours, and he became world famous after the flight.
items.q: What did Charles Lindbergh do in 1927?
o: He flew alone from New York to Paris.
items.ex: ニューヨークからパリまで、1人で無着陸飛行をしました。

lines: Sophie works as a nurse at a large hospital. She often works at night, so it is difficult for her to meet her friends. To keep in touch, she started a group chat with them. Now they share photos and plan to meet on her days off.
items.q: Why is it difficult for Sophie to meet her friends?
items.ex: She often works at night とあります。

lines: Thank you for calling City Gas. If you smell gas in your home, please hang up and call our emergency number right away. For questions about your bill, press 1. To start or stop service, press 2. For all other questions, please stay on the line.
items.q: What should callers do if they smell gas?
items.ex: ガスのにおいがしたら、電話を切って緊急番号にかけます。

lines: Last year, Ms. Yamada opened a café where customers can read books for free. She wanted to create a quiet place for people who live alone. Many older people in the neighborhood now visit every day, and some have become good friends.
items.q: Why did Ms. Yamada open the café?
o: To create a quiet place for people who live alone.
To make a lot of money.
items.ex: She wanted to create a quiet place for people who live alone. とあります。

lines: The Seikan Tunnel connects Honshu and Hokkaido under the sea. It is about 54 kilometers long, and about 23 kilometers of it is under the seabed. It took more than 20 years to build, and it opened in 1988. Today, Hokkaido Shinkansen trains run through it.
items.q: What does the Seikan Tunnel connect?
items.ex: connects Honshu and Hokkaido under the sea とあります。

lines: Good afternoon, shoppers. Our store will hold a special event this Saturday. The famous chef Ken Mori will show how to cook easy dishes using seasonal vegetables. The event starts at 2 p.m. on the first floor, and it is free to watch.
items.q: What will happen on Saturday?
o: A chef will show how to cook.
items.ex: 有名シェフが料理のしかたを見せるイベントがあります。

lines: Takumi has loved drawing comics since he was a child. In high school, he sent his comics to a publisher many times, but they were always rejected. He kept trying, and at the age of 22, one of his stories was finally published in a magazine.
items.q: What happened when Takumi was 22?
o: One of his stories was published.
items.ex: at the age of 22, one of his stories was finally published とあります。

lines: Cherry trees in Japan bloom at different times depending on the area. In Okinawa, they bloom in January, while in Hokkaido, people usually have to wait until May. Every year, weather companies announce forecasts showing when the flowers will open in each city.
items.q: When do cherry trees usually bloom in Hokkaido?
items.ex: in Hokkaido, people usually have to wait until May とあります。1月は沖縄です。

lines: Attention, passengers. This bus will make a ten-minute stop at the next rest area. Please make sure to return to the bus by 3:20. The bus will leave on time, so please do not be late. Thank you.
items.q: What should passengers do?

items.ex: Please make sure to return to the bus by 3:20. とあります。

lines: Lucas started working at a hotel in Kyoto last year. Many guests asked him about places to visit, but he did not know much about the city. So he began spending his days off visiting temples and restaurants. Now guests often thank him for his helpful advice.

o: He wanted to give guests better advice.
He wanted to find a new job.
items.ex: お客さんに聞かれても答えられなかったので、休みの日に見て回るようになりました。
